title: Constraint-driven OKRs: weekly scratch & micro-retros
content:
Purpose:
I want a compact, repeatable weekly scratch that treats constraints (time, attention, compute budget) as the primary lever for shaping OKRs.

Context note to self: previously I tracked too many KRs; they became todo lists rather than evaluative signals. This doc is an experimental template and running log for the next 8 weeks. Keep it small, measurable, and constraint-aware.

Sprint window: 2026-02-22 -> 2026-03-07 (two-week micro-sprint)
Primary constraint this sprint: personal weekly deep-focus time = 6hrs
Secondary constraint: compute spend cap for hosted experiments = $120

Top-level objectives (constraint-framed):
1) Reduce token cost variance on top-15 routes by 20% within compute cap
   - KR1.1: Implement prefix cache for 5 highest-volume routes (target 15% cost delta)
   - KR1.2: Add batching tweaks + new client-side debounce: reduce calls by 12%
2) Raise confidence in rollout gating heuristics so can do daily canaries
   - KR2.1: Build 2 synthetic prompt suites that surface regressions within 10 requests
   - KR2.2: Add latency heatmap per route in console, show delta vs baseline
3) Personal craft: ship 1 reproducible eval + write-up for the team (30–45m read)

Weekly check-ins (short):
- Week start (Mon): pick 3 focus slots (2x 90m, 1x 120m). Block calendar.
- Midweek: quick metric sanity check; note what drained attention.
- End: 20m retro + next sprint planning.

This sprint log (notes / micro actions):
- 2026-02-23: Blocked 2x 90m focus. Did prefix cache spike prototype using local model runner; got ~9% improvement on small sample. Questions: reproducible at scale? Needs batch integration.
- 2026-02-25: Spent 60m pairing with Jordan on debounce heuristics. Agreed to toggle client debounce per route. Opened jira/RED-3421.
- 2026-02-27: Quick console mock — latency heatmap: showing high tail on route /chat-stream. Hypothesis: network + small batch sizes.

Mini-retro (end of week):
- Wins: small prototype demonstrated measurable delta with low effort; got early buy-in.
- Misses: lost an afternoon to triage unrelated infra alert (interrupt cost). Plan: escalate pager routing with SRE to reduce interruptions.
- What to remove next sprint: low-impact metrics (per-token averages across all routes) -> focus per-route 95thpct and cost-per-session.

Hypotheses to test next sprint (clear pass/fail criteria):
H1: Applying prefix cache + 2x debounce reduces median cost per session by >=12% (pass = observed reduction in production-like replay).
H2: Introducing route-level debounce will not increase user-perceived latency for 95% of sessions (pass = <1% sessions with latency > baseline+150ms).

Failure modes & mitigations (quick list):
- Cache correctness: risk of stale responses -> mitigation: conservative TTL + validation suite in synthetic prompts.
- Over-batching: risk of increased tail latency -> mitigation: dynamic batch size cap and fallback to small-batch fast path.
- Personal overcommit: risk of burnout -> mitigation: hard limit on focus hours; delegate pairing work.

Quarterly signals I care about (how I'll know this worked):
- Cost per active session down 10–20% on targeted routes
- Fewer manual rollbacks during peak (2->0 per month)
- A concrete reproducible eval that the team can run and discuss in 1-hour sync

Actionable next steps (first 7 days):
1) Write short README for prefix cache prototype + steps to run (2hrs). -> task assigned to me.
2) Create synthetic prompt suite draft (3hrs) and ask Aisha for edge-case inputs.
3) Draft rollout policy update for canaries (30m) and link to github PR.
4) Escalate pager routing to SRE (10m chat)

Notes-to-self (loose):
- When things feel busy: check if interrupt is part of a constraint violation (attention/time) and reassign.
- Keep the KRs evaluative: if a KR looks like a checklist, rewrite it into a metric + threshold.

Open questions (to bring up in 1:1):
- Can we get an extra $200 compute buffer if a hypothesis needs a larger replay? (ask for temporary lift)
- Who owns per-route debounce default values — product or SDK? Need clarity to avoid thrash.

Quick template for next weekly note (copy this into next doc):
- Sprint window:
- Constraint(s):
- Primary KRs (with metrics):
- 3 focus slots this week:
- Weekly log (3 bullet days):
- Mini-retro (win/miss/remove):
- Hypotheses for next sprint:
- 3 immediate actions:

End of scratch. Keep short and iterative. If this becomes long, split into a dedicated PRD or eval notebook and move polished content to Confluence.
